question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $70u+25v=\text{gcd}(70,25).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}70 & = & 25\cdot 2 & + & 20 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 25 & = & 20\cdot 1 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 20 & = & 5\cdot 4 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(70,25)=5.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & =70-2\cdot 25 \\ 5 & =25-20.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =25-20 \\  & =25-(70-2\cdot 25) \\  & =25\cdot 3-70 \\  & =70\cdot (-1)+25\cdot 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-1$ and $v=3.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-1)+3=2.
$$
